title: Unveiling Temperature-Driven Phase Separation of Completely Miscible Au-Pd Alloys: An In-Situ TEM Insights
content: Research in plasmonic noble metal nanomaterials (NMN) observed a spike recently due to their extraordinary optical properties compared to their bulk counterparts. The ability to generate hot electrons and holes during interaction with external electromagnetic waves makes them suitable to initiate chemical reaction at their surfaces using external excitations (especially light or electron beam) and they already showed potential to replace fossil fuels in near future. [1-3] In this aspect, bimetallic nanoparticles have garnered significant attention due to their superior efficiency in heterogeneous catalysis. These systems exhibit enhanced stability and catalytic activity compared to their individual metallic counterparts. In this context, Au@Pd core-shell nanoparticles and Au-Pd nano-alloys have been explored for electrocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production and ethanol oxidation reactions, demonstrating significantly improved catalytic performance compared to bare Pd nanoparticles. However, while Au nanoparticles are highly efficient in converting alcohols to aldehydes, they are less effective for oxygen reduction—an activity in which Pd excels. By alloying Au and Pd, these limitations can be mitigated; however, the lower electrochemical potential of the alloy compared to the individual metals reduces its efficiency in alcohol-to-aldehyde conversion.
